title: Isotopes: same element, different neutrons
examples: Why is chlorine 35.5 on the periodic table?

explain.say: Imagine twins who look the same and act the same, but one is a little heavier. Atoms can have twins like that too! Look at the board: you can see two kinds of carbon atom, side by side.
See carbon-12 on the left? It has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. The 12 is its mass number, protons plus neutrons. Almost all the carbon in you is this kind. Can you add 6 and 6 to check?

Now look at carbon-14 on the right. Still 6 protons, so it is still carbon. But it has 8 neutrons, so it is heavier. Atoms of one element with different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes. Can you count how many extra neutrons it has?

Two! Now look at the reasons on the board. Reactions are all about electrons, and isotopes have the same electrons. Only the mass is different. So carbon-14 burns just like carbon-12. Does that make sense to you?

because.label: Same electrons
because.ask: Why do isotopes react the same way?

draw.answer: Isotopes have the same electrons, so they react the same

explain.say: Great work! Carbon-14 is radioactive, which means its nucleus slowly breaks down. Half of it is gone after about 5,730 years. Wow: by measuring what is left, you can date ancient wooden tools and Egyptian mummies.

faq.a: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. So they have different mass numbers.

faq.q: Why do isotopes react the same way?
faq.a: Chemical reactions depend on electrons. Isotopes of an element have the same number of electrons, so they react in the same way.
asks: Do isotopes have the same chemical properties?

faq.a: Living things take in carbon-14 while alive. After death it decays, halving about every 5,730 years, so measuring what is left shows the age, up to about 50,000 years.

faq.q: Why is chlorine's relative atomic mass 35.5?
faq.a: Chlorine is a mix of two isotopes: about three quarters chlorine-35 and one quarter chlorine-37. The average mass works out at about 35.5.
asks: Why are some atomic masses not whole numbers?

faq.a: No. Many isotopes, like carbon-12 and carbon-13, are stable. Others, like carbon-14 and uranium-235, are radioactive and slowly decay.

facts: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years.
Natural chlorine is about 75.8 percent chlorine-35 and 24.2 percent chlorine-37, giving a relative atomic mass of about 35.5.

quiz.say: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 have different numbers of which particle?
quiz.show: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 have different numbers of which particle?
quiz.why: Isotopes differ only in their number of neutrons: 18 and 20 here.

wrong.0: Both have 17 protons, or they would not be chlorine.
wrong.1: Neutral atoms of both have 17 electrons.

quiz.say: A sample is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
quiz.show: A sample is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
quiz.why: 0.75 times 35 plus 0.25 times 37 is 26.25 plus 9.25, which is 35.5.

wrong.0: You take a weighted average, not a sum.
wrong.2: 36 is a plain average; more atoms are chlorine-35, so it is lower.
